﻿Practice Test 1

Instructions:
Choose one answer for each question. Each question has four options: A, B, C and D. The answer key is provided at the end.
1. A business analyst finds that sales records are held in five different spreadsheets with different product names. What is the best first action?
A. Create a shared data dictionary and standard naming rules *
B. Merge the spreadsheets without checking them
C. Delete the smallest spreadsheet
D. Ask each team to keep using its own format

2. An organisation wants to store both raw web logs and cleaned reporting data. Which design is most suitable?
A. A single desktop spreadsheet
B. A data lakehouse or combined storage and analytics platform *
C. An email inbox
D. A presentation file

3. A cloud database automatically increases compute capacity during high demand. Which benefit does this describe?
A. Data masking
B. Normalisation
C. Scalability *
D. Manual governance

4. A team needs quick summary reports showing revenue by region, product and month. Which system is most appropriate?
A. Word processor
B. Flat text editor
C. Image library
D. OLAP or data warehouse *

5. You are comparing a relational database with object storage for transaction data. What is a key strength of the relational database?
A. It supports structured tables, relationships and SQL queries *
B. It is best for storing unstructured videos only
C. It removes the need for data quality checks

6. A dataset contains customer ages, income and spending score. You want to group similar customers without a target label. Which technique should you use?
A. Linear regression
B. Clustering *
C. Confusion matrix
D. Hypothesis testing

A. Accuracy
B. F1 score
C. Mean Absolute Error *
D. Confusion matrix

8. A classifier identifies fraud cases, but fraud is very rare. Why might accuracy be misleading?
A. Accuracy always ignores correct predictions
B. Accuracy only works with text data
C. Accuracy cannot be calculated for binary models
D. A model can look accurate by predicting the majority class *

9. A model performs well during development but poorly after deployment because customer behaviour has changed. What is the likely issue?
A. Concept drift *
B. Data duplication
C. One hot encoding
D. Indexing

10. A bank wants to explain why a machine learning model rejected a loan application. Which approach is most useful?
A. Removing the applicant record
B. Model explainability techniques such as SHAP *
C. Increasing the number of hidden layers only
D. Changing the file name

11. A dataset has missing values in income because some high earners refuse to disclose it. What should you do first?
A. Replace all missing values with zero
B. Delete the income column immediately
C. Treat the missingness as potentially systematic *
D. Assume the values are randomly missing

12. A numeric feature ranges from 0 to 1,000,000 while another ranges from 0 to 1. Which preprocessing step may help many algorithms?
A. Adding more rows manually
B. Removing the target variable
C. Creating a pie chart

13. A dataset includes job title as a categorical variable. What is a common way to prepare it for many machine learning models?
A. One hot encoding *
B. Removing all rows
C. Sorting alphabetically only

14. A team trains a model using future information that would not be available at prediction time. What problem has occurred?
A. Sampling error only
B. Data leakage *
C. Data compression
D. Normalisation

15. An analyst wants to test whether a marketing campaign changed average spend. Which method is most appropriate?
A. Image recognition
B. K means clustering
C. Hypothesis test comparing means *
D. Min max scaling

16. A scatterplot shows that as advertising spend increases, sales usually increase. What relationship is being observed?

D. Positive correlation *

18. A business asks for a dashboard for senior leaders who need a quick performance overview. What should you prioritise?

D. Unlabelled charts

19. A model is too complex and performs much better on training data than test data. What is the most likely issue?
A. Underfitting
B. Correct sampling
C. Overfitting *
D. Perfect generalisation

20. A decision tree is chosen over a deep neural network for a simple business rule problem. What is a likely reason?
A. It never overfits

21. You need to process streaming sensor readings and update alerts quickly. What type of processing is most suitable?

B. Annual manual reporting only
C. Printing the data

22. A data pipeline fails because the source system changed a column name. What would help prevent unnoticed failures?

23. Which activity best supports data governance?

D. Copying files to personal drives

24. An analyst wants to reduce 80 related variables into fewer components while retaining much of the variation. Which technique could be used?

D. Principal Component Analysis *

25. A retailer wants to recommend products based on similar customer behaviour. Which analytical approach is most relevant?

B. Text spellchecking only
C. Manual filing
D. Data deletion

C. Whether emails are archived
D. Whether the data is stored in PDF only

Instructions:

D. Source control

17. A binary classifier threshold is raised from 0.5 to 0.8. What is a likely effect?

18. A project team wants to make results reproducible. What should they record?
